messages:
elaine_ops: Heads up — getting a burst of GPU pod evictions in us-west1 right now (~10:22 PT). Eviction spikes correlate with lots of Pending -> CrashLoop cycles. Noticed higher latebind failures in the logs. Anyone else seeing this?

simon_infra: yep saw the alert. packing fragmentation in gpu-pool-usw1-az3 jumped from 18% -> 42% around the same time.

maria_scheduler: looking at scheduler logs, a bunch of pods hit BindTimeout: lease failed when talking to control-plane egress (metadata K8S API) — binder retried and then preemption/requeue happened.

samir_sre: control-plane egress had a short tail latency spike to our metadata enip (10.22.14.0/24). 503s from our AGW for ~90s starting at 10:21:58. Might be rate limiting on the host egress path.

leo_infra: confirmed netstats on the affected rack show retransmits and tcp_sndbuf growth. Looks like congestion on the rack Egress NIC.

elaine_ops: tl;dr: scheduler backoff + latebind timeouts -> repeated binds -> evict churn -> fragmentation increases -> more Pending. vicious loop.

maria_scheduler: quick data dump from one scheduler instance: 
```
I0315 10:22:03.123456 1 binder.go:412] BindTimeout pod/llm-train-105: lease allocate failed: metadata request timeout
I0315 10:22:04.231000 1 scheduler_cache.go:231] Pod llm-train-105 moved to pending, preempt attempt
I0315 10:22:05.412345 1 eviction.go:78] evicting pod llm-train-101 -> node drain
```

samir_sre: immediate mitigation I applied: bumped scheduler BindTimeout from 5s -> 15s on canary schedulers, and paused the aggressive preempt policy for 60s. Deploy-bot scaled the warm pool +2 nodes in the affected AZ.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled gpu-warmpool-usw1-az3 by +2 (from 6 -> 8) per request by @samir_sre :robot_face:  

leo_infra: also cleared a stale egress ACL rule that was causing asymmetric routing; rollback would have been messy so we removed the rule and started flow pinning for the rack.

elaine_ops: after the timeout bump and warmpool +2, fragmentation dropped from 42% -> 26% in ~6m, and eviction rate dropped to baseline. Good sign but still brittle.

maria_scheduler: long term fixes we should consider:
- make latebind idempotent (fast failover to alternate metadata endpoint)
- move lease handshake off critical egress path (local cached tokens + async refresh)
- add backoff hysteresis to eviction workflow so a single bind failure doesn't immediately trigger preemption
- run a defrag job that opportunistically coalesces tiny pods into warm nodes during quiet windows

samir_sre: agree. Also add a circuit-breaker on control-plane egress: if x% of binds fail in 60s, increase timeouts and pause preemption automatically.

leo_infra: cost note — warmpool +2 is ~0.6 GPU-hours/minute extra. If we do automated pauses often, we need guardrails to avoid extra monthly cost.

elaine_ops: action items: @maria_scheduler put the BindTimeout change into a small rollout (15s default) and add a metric for bind-failure-rate to trigger auto-hysteresis. @leo_infra double-check egress ACLs for the other racks in us-west1. @samir_sre write runbook snippet for this churn. I'll monitor for 2 hours.

maria_scheduler: acked, will open a PR for the timeout + metric and tag for a canary.

samir_sre: adding a short runbook note here: 
"If you see GPU pod evict surge + bind errors: 1) bump bind timeout to 15s on canary schedulers 2) pause preempt policy 3) scale warmpool +1..3 4) check rack egress ACLs and NIC errors"

elaine_ops: thanks team. dropping charts in #observability in case we need them. :thumbsup:

maria_scheduler: postmortem candidate if recurs — repeated loop makes for a solid postmortem.

samir_sre: will follow up with metric alert that auto-triggers hysteresis.

leo_infra: RTG on ACL sweep now.

deploy-bot: note: change to BindTimeout canary rolled to 2 schedulers (us-west1-canary-1/2). Monitor CPU & schedule latency for 15m.
